limitations_and_boundaries: The study does not include in vivo metastasis data for the G3BP2 knockdown condition in the provided chunks; only the xenograft model is mentioned without results.
The mechanism of stiffness-induced phosphorylation of TWIST1 Tyr107 is inferred from in vitro data and mass spectrometry of a different cell line.

missed_core_items.description: The study includes a key result that matrix stiffness alone does not induce a complete EMT; a full EMT requires both high stiffness and TGF-β. This is a central finding that is not captured in the extracted items.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: As high stiﬀness alone was not suﬃcient to induce a complete EMT (Fig. 1f), we investigated whether TWIST1 is also required for the induction of a full EMT by mechanical signals in concert with the EMT-inducing biochemical signal TGF-β (ref. 33).

missed_core_items.description: The study demonstrates that TWIST1 nuclear localization is regulated by a distinct mechanotransduction pathway independent of YAP, using micropatterning and leptomycin B experiments. This is a core mechanistic finding not represented in the extraction.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: TWIST1 nuclear localization was not aﬀected by changes in cell shape in either MCF10A or Eph4Ras cells (Fig. 3b–d and Supplementary Fig. 2).

missed_core_items.description: The study includes a key result that β1-integrin blocking antibody prevents TWIST1 nuclear translocation, linking integrin activation to TWIST1 mechanoregulation. This is a core experimental finding omitted from the extraction.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Treatment with a β1-integrin-blocking antibody (AIIB2) prevented nuclear translocation of TWIST1 and blocked the invasive phenotype induced by high matrix stiﬀness1,2 (Fig. 3a), further supporting a critical role for TWIST1 in mediating matrix-stiﬀness-induced EMT and invasion.

missed_core_items.description: The study includes a key result that G3BP2 knockdown does not affect YAP localization, supporting distinct mechanoregulation. This is a core finding not captured.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: In further support of distinct mechanoregulation of TWIST1 and YAP, knockdown of G3BP2 did not aﬀect YAP localization (Supplementary Fig. 4D).

missed_core_items.description: The study includes a key result that G3BP2 knockdown in MCF10DCIS xenografts leads to increased lung metastasis (15- and 65-fold). This is a central quantitative in vivo result omitted from the extraction.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: tumours expressing G3BP2 shRNAs consistently presented with a striking increase in the number of distant metastases in the lungs compared with tumours expressing a control shRNA (mean increase: 15- and 65-fold for G3BP2 shRNA6 and shRNA8 versus control, respectively; Fig. 6g,h).

missed_core_items.description: The study includes a key result that G3BP2 expression is restricted to luminal epithelial cells in normal human breast and colon tissues. This is a core finding for the clinical relevance.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: consistent with a role in preventing EMT and invasion, we observed that G3BP2 protein expression was restricted to the luminal epithelial cells in normal human breast and colon tissues (Fig. 7a and Supplementary Fig. 6D).

missed_core_items.description: The study includes a key result that combined low G3BP2 and organized collagen (high stiffness) predicts poor recurrence-free survival in stage-3 breast cancer patients (10-year survival 10.1% vs 46.4%). This is a central clinical finding omitted.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Patients with disorganized collagen/G3BP2high tumours had markedly improved outcomes with a 10-year recurrence-free survival rate of 46.4% compared with 10.1% of patients with organized collagen/G3BP2low tumours.

research_questions.statement: How are mechanical inputs from matrix stiffness transduced into transcriptional outputs to drive tumour progression?

experiments_or_tasks: MCF10DCIS xenograft model with G3bp2 knockdown to assess tumour invasion and metastasis.

methods.name: Xenograft tumour model
methods.protocol_description: MCF10DCIS cells with G3bp2 knockdown were injected into mice to form tumours; invasion and metastasis were analyzed.

study_units.name: Loss of G3BP2 promotes tumour invasion and metastasis in vivo

provenance.text_excerpt: These data indicate that G3BP2 directly impacts EMT and invasion in response to matrix stiﬀness and provide a mechanism by which the TWIST1–G3BP2 mechanotransduction pathway can facilitate tumour invasion.

claims.statement: G3BP2 is required for cytoplasmic retention of TWIST1 at low stiffness; its loss cooperates with increasing stiffness to promote EMT and invasion in a Twist1-dependent manner.

experiments_or_tasks: Culture of Eph4Ras cells on stiffness gradient (150-5,700 Pa) with G3bp2 knockdown to measure invasion and EMT markers.
Double knockdown of Twist1 and G3bp2 to test dependency.
Knockdown of G3BP2 in MCF10A and Eph4Ras cells on compliant matrices to assess TWIST1 localization.

methods.name: 3D culture on stiffness gradient
methods.protocol_description: Eph4Ras cells were cultured on polyacrylamide hydrogels with elasticities from 150 Pa to 5,700 Pa.

methods.name: shRNA knockdown of G3BP2
methods.protocol_description: G3BP2 was knocked down using shRNAs; knockdown efficiency was confirmed.

study_units.name: Loss of G3BP2 cooperates with stiffness to promote TWIST1 nuclear localization and EMT

provenance.text_excerpt: knockdown of G3BP2 resulted in nuclear accumulation of TWIST1

results.value_raw_text: Knockdown of G3BP2 resulted in nuclear accumulation of TWIST1 on compliant matrices in MCF10A and Eph4Ras cells.

provenance.text_excerpt: G3bp2 knockdown repressed expression of E-cadherin and induced expression of vimentin

results.value_raw_text: G3bp2 knockdown repressed E-cadherin and induced vimentin expression.

provenance.text_excerpt: we knocked down both Twist1 and G3bp2 and found that the EMT and invasive phenotype were significantly suppressed compared with cells that were depleted of only G3bp2

results.value_raw_text: Double knockdown of Twist1 and G3bp2 significantly suppressed EMT and invasive phenotype compared to G3bp2 knockdown alone.

provenance.text_excerpt: G3bp2 knockdown and the resulting constitutive Twist1 nuclear localization significantly increased the percentage of invasive acini at matrix rigidities ranging from 150 Pa to 670 Pa. Importantly, loss of G3bp2 and increasing matrix stiﬀness synergistically resulted in destabilization of basement membrane, an EMT phenotype and invasion

results.value_raw_text: G3bp2 knockdown significantly increased the percentage of invasive acini at 150-670 Pa; loss of G3bp2 and increasing stiffness synergistically destabilized basement membrane and induced EMT.

provenance.text_excerpt: Snai2, a direct transcription target of TWIST1, was induced following G3bp2 knockdown; in contrast, double knockdown of G3bp2 and Twist1 blocked Snai2 induction

results.value_raw_text: Snai2 was induced following G3bp2 knockdown; double knockdown of G3bp2 and Twist1 blocked Snai2 induction.

provenance.text_excerpt: These data strongly suggest that increasing matrix stiﬀness could disrupt Twist1–G3BP2 binding through phosphorylation of Tyr 107 within the G3BP2-binding motif of Twist1.

claims.statement: G3BP2 binds TWIST1 through a conserved motif and matrix stiffness disrupts this interaction, possibly via phosphorylation of Tyr107.

experiments_or_tasks: Co-immunoprecipitation of endogenous TWIST1 and G3BP2.
Phospho-mimetic Y107E mutant to test phosphorylation effect on binding.
Proximity ligation assay (PLA) to detect Twist1-G3bp2 interaction at 150 Pa vs 5,700 Pa in 3D acini and single cells.
Sequence alignment to identify G3BP2-binding motif in TWIST1.

methods.name: Co-immunoprecipitation
methods.protocol_description: Endogenous and exogenously expressed TWIST1 were immunoprecipitated and probed for G3BP2.

methods.name: Proximity ligation assay (PLA)
methods.protocol_description: In situ PLA using antibodies against Twist1 and G3bp2 in 3D acinar cultures and single cells.

methods.name: Mutagenesis
methods.protocol_description: Deletion of G3BP2-binding motif (1QT) and point mutations Y107F and Y107E were generated.

study_units.name: G3BP2 binds TWIST1 and mediates stiffness-regulated localization

provenance.text_excerpt: We confirmed that both endogenously and exogenously expressed TWIST1 co-immunoprecipitated with endogenous G3BP2

results.value_raw_text: Endogenous and exogenous TWIST1 co-immunoprecipitated with endogenous G3BP2.

provenance.text_excerpt: PLA analysis in single cells detected strong interaction between G3bp2 and Twist1 in the cytoplasm at low stiﬀness, but not at high stiﬀness

results.value_raw_text: Single cells showed strong interaction between G3bp2 and Twist1 in cytoplasm at low stiffness, but not at high stiffness.

provenance.text_excerpt: Deletion of this motif (1QT mutant) in Twist1 abolished its interaction with G3BP2

results.value_raw_text: Deletion of the motif (1QT mutant) abolished interaction with G3BP2.

provenance.text_excerpt: the phospho-deficient Y107F Twist1 mutant co-immunoprecipitated with G3BP2 with similar eﬃciency as wild-type Twist1 but the interaction between the phospho-mimetic Y107E Twist1 mutant and G3BP2 was markedly attenuated

results.value_raw_text: Y107F mutant co-immunoprecipitated with G3BP2 similarly to wild-type; Y107E mutant interaction was markedly attenuated.

provenance.text_excerpt: at 150 Pa a strong PLA signal, indicating Twist1/G3bp2 interaction, was specifically enriched in the cytoplasm. In contrast, very little PLA signal was detected at 5,700 Pa

results.value_raw_text: Strong PLA signal (Twist1/G3bp2 interaction) at 150 Pa in cytoplasm; very little signal at 5,700 Pa.

provenance.text_excerpt: Sequence alignment of this G3BP2-interacting region of NFKBIA with TWIST1 and MDM2 revealed a consensus G3BP2-binding motif, Q-X-X-X-E-L-Q-[ET]-X-[KR]-[LPV]

results.value_raw_text: A consensus G3BP2-binding motif Q-X-X-X-E-L-Q-[ET]-X-[KR]-[LPV] was identified in TWIST1, conserved in vertebrate Twist1.

provenance.text_excerpt: Together, these data indicate an essential role for TWIST1 in mediating matrix-stiﬀness-induced EMT and invasion.

Treatment with TGF-β on soft (150 Pa) and rigid (5,700 Pa) matrices to test synergy with TWIST1.
